sections.h2: Where is West Haven, Connecticut, and what are its borders?
sections.html:
West Haven is a coastal city in New Haven County on Long Island Sound, directly west of New Haven across the West River.

The city covers about 11 square miles and had 55,584 residents in 2020. The Oyster River marks the boundary with Milford on the southwest, Orange lies to the northwest and New Haven to the north. New Haven Harbor is to the east and the Sound is to the south, and the Cove River runs through town.

West Haven has 3.5 miles of public beaches, about one quarter of the public beach in Connecticut. The city is part of the South Central Connecticut Planning Region and has a mayor-council government. Wikipedia lists Dorinda Borer as mayor.

sections.h2: What are the neighborhoods and fire districts in West Haven?
sections.html:
West Haven's three main communities are Allingtown, West Shore and the Center, and Sandy Point is a smaller area on the harbor.

The communities line up with the fire districts, which matters for a seller because the districts have levied their own taxes. Wikipedia reports that the Allingtown district was folded into the city, while the First Fire Taxation (Center) and West Shore districts each still set their own tax rate. It also notes the state's Municipal Accountability Review Board has been giving the city financial guidance.

  • Allingtown: the hilly area that holds the University of New Haven.
  • West Shore: the shoreline area along the Sound.
  • Center: the West Haven Green, Campbell Avenue and the Main Street area.
  • Sandy Point: a beach and bird sanctuary reaching into New Haven Harbor.

Because a fire district tax can change a bill, ask the tax office which district your address falls in and what you owe to each. Wikipedia also notes that West Haven originally had three fire districts served by the West Haven, West Shore and Allingtown fire departments, so older paperwork may use those names.

West Haven was settled in 1648 as West Farms, became its own parish in 1719, split from Orange as a separate town in 1921 and was incorporated as a city in 1961.

That last date earned it the label "Connecticut's Youngest City," even though it is one of the state's oldest settlements. Shipping drove the early economy, followed by buckle and button shops, piano and organ makers and, in World War II, an Armstrong Rubber plant that made tires and rafts.

Savin Rock was a seaside resort by the 1870s and a regional amusement park into the 1960s. Redevelopment fights lasted about 40 years, and in 2007 a conservation easement protected the shoreline parks as open space. Lender's Bagels began here in 1927. The Bayer pharmaceutical campus closed after 2006 and Yale University bought the 137-acre site in 2007 for research use.

sections.h2: What do West Haven's demographics and housing counts say?
sections.html:
The 2020 Census counted 21,409 households and 22,735 housing units in West Haven, with 5.8% of units vacant.

About 31.4% of households were one person living alone, and 36.0% were married-couple households. The 2020 count also shows 18.8% of residents under 18 and 15.9% age 65 or older, which gives a sense of how many households may be downsizing or inheriting.

sections.h2: How does the coast affect owning and selling a house in West Haven?
sections.html:
A West Haven house near the water has a different set of concerns than one on Allingtown Hill.

The city's elevation is listed at 33 feet, and the shoreline runs along both New Haven Harbor and the Sound. Flood risk differs by address, so look up your lot on the FEMA flood map and ask the city's building department about any flood zone rules before you set an asking price.

Since 2020, some West Shore residents have reported a persistent humming noise, and the city set aside $16,000 in January 2026 to find the source, according to Wikipedia's citations of the New Haven Register and the New York Times. If you own in that area, a buyer may ask about it.

sections.h2: How do roads, rail and schools connect West Haven?
sections.html:
Interstate 95, Route 34 (Derby Avenue) and US Route 1 all cross West Haven, between Orange and New Haven.

The Metro-North West Haven station opened in 2013 on the New Haven Line, with 660 parking spaces and full service to New York. Amtrak does not stop in West Haven, so the nearest Amtrak stop is New Haven Union Station. Tweed New Haven Regional Airport is the closest air service, and CT Transit buses run along Campbell Avenue and Orange Avenue.

West Haven has one public high school, a middle school, an intermediate school and six elementary schools, plus three private schools. The University of New Haven and a Veterans Affairs hospital are also in the city, and Yale's athletic fields and West Campus extend into town.

sections.h2: What taxes and filings apply when you sell in West Haven?
sections.html:
The seller or the seller's attorney files Connecticut Form OP-236 for the conveyance tax when the deed is recorded with the West Haven town clerk.

Under the state Department of Revenue Services rules, tax is due when the price is $2,000 or more unless an exemption applies, and West Haven's town code is 156. The state lists exemptions such as a deed in lieu of foreclosure on a principal residence and a sale of a principal residence where the price cannot cover the mortgages and priority taxes. Ask the office, and ask which fire district bills your address.

  • Request a payoff of real estate and fire district taxes before closing.
  • Ask whether a lien or open code issue is on record.
  • Confirm whether a bank escrow account pays your bills.

sections.h2: What do West Haven sellers often face, and what are the options?
sections.html:
West Haven sellers choose among a listing, a private sale and a cash offer, usually depending on repairs, tax balances and timing.

  • Waterfront and near-shore houses that need storm or moisture repairs.
  • Two- and three-family houses with tenants.
  • Inherited houses where an estate has not yet been settled.
  • Owners behind on city or fire district taxes who need closing money fast.

A cash purchase generally closes without a lender appraisal, which can shorten the schedule. Compare any offer to what a traditional sale would net after commission, repairs and carrying costs, and decide from there.

faqs.q: What county is West Haven in?
faqs.a: West Haven is in New Haven County, on Long Island Sound. Deeds are recorded with the West Haven town clerk, since Connecticut has no county recording office.

faqs.q: How many people live in West Haven?
faqs.a: The 2020 Census counted 55,584 residents in West Haven, living in 21,409 households.

faqs.q: Does West Haven have separate fire district taxes?
faqs.a: Wikipedia reports that the First Fire Taxation (Center) and West Shore districts each levy their own tax rate, and the Allingtown district was absorbed by the city. Ask the tax office which district applies to your house.

faqs.q: What is the conveyance tax form for a West Haven sale?
faqs.a: The seller files Connecticut Form OP-236 when the deed is recorded, and West Haven's town code on the form is 156. Tax is due on transfers of $2,000 or more unless an exemption applies.

faqs.q: Can I sell a West Haven house that has storm damage or tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. You can sell as-is to a cash buyer or list after repairs. Give any buyer a clear picture of the damage, tenants and open balances before you agree to a price.
